scope: Proposition 5.1 (Small sausage values are unlikely) of the manuscript “An explicit exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE” (preprints/An-explicit-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-26-2026/An-explicit-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-26-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 230 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c6e7116ea33f29ee), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every deterministic J = [s, t] with 0 ≤ s < t < ∞, lim a↓0 lim sup e↓0 P{Xe(J) < a} = 0. (5.5) Equivalently, for every ε > 0 there are a, e0 > 0 such that P{Xe(J) < a} < ε for all 0 < e < e0. The same conclusion can be required simultaneously for any fixed finite list of such intervals, with total exceptional probability as small as desired.
